surfaces.part: hanging rock cliff faces below the ledges

answer.evidence: This is a terrain autotile of a floating void platform. The large cobbled floor (rows 17-93) is a horizontal top surface that ends in a light front-edge line at about row 94, with darker rock rows below. The same pattern repeats on the middle ledge (edge line at row 78) and the right ledge (edge line at row 46). Each ledge has a hanging, tapering cliff face of about 20 rows beneath its edge line that fades into the dark void. No isometric side face is drawn. The south face is a normal front cliff, so the piece reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a void-edge floating-platform patch in purples. It shows about 4-5 value steps: a light purple lip highlight, mid purple top, darker speckled rock, deep cliff underside and near-void background. Measured facts: 5 visible tones per tile (reference grass 3, paving 7), 5% near-flat coverage (references 0%), and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the edges lean purple rather than neutral black. The top surface has scattered speckle dots and cracks, and the cliff faces have stone-like blocks, so it avoids large flat fills. However, only 6 raw colours per tile and 10 in total make the grain sparse and uniform next to the grass reference's 26 per tile and 80 overall. The speckle is a low-contrast noise pattern rather than per-stone shading or clumped tufts, so it is somewhat thinner than the paving reference. The cliff undersides also read as fairly flat. It is acceptable on tinted outlines and passable density, but still a bit thinner than the references.

answer.evidence: The tile is a large purple stone floor seen from above (rows 17-94). It ends in bright 1-row front-edge lines at rows 94-95 on the left, row 79 in the middle and row 46 on the upper right. Each is followed by a darker rocky cliff face of about 15-20 rows that tapers downward into void (e.g. rows 96-115 on the left). The inner ledges at rows 46 and 79 repeat the same top-plus-cliff structure. This is a top surface with a front face of 3+ rows, so it reads as three-quarter terrain.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a purple void-edge floating slab with speckled rock texture, lighter ledge lips, and dark underside stalactites. Measured: 5 visible tones per tile (grass ref 3, paving ref 7), 5% near-flat coverage (refs 0%), 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the edges are tinted purple and not a black sticker line. Shading is about 4 steps (dark base, mid purple, light speckle, bright ledge lip), a little shallower than Beodeul's 5-6 per material. Raw colours are only 10 in total and 6 per tile, which makes the rock face repetitive: scattered dots over a nearly uniform base, with few individually shaded stones. It sits between the two references on tones and is not flat, but it is slightly thinner than the paving reference and lacks per-stone shading. Taken together this is borderline, and when in doubt it fails.

surfaces.part: cliff front faces below the ledges (dithered rock fading to void)

answer.evidence: The floor plateau fills rows 17-93 as a large horizontal surface with a rocky texture. It ends in a light front-edge line at rows 94-95 (#8462d6 at row 95), then darker shadow rows. Below that is a vertical cliff face of about 17 rows that fades into the dark void. The center ledge (edge line rows 78-79) and the upper-right ledge (edge line rows 46-47) repeat the same pattern: a top surface, an edge line, then a cliff face. The camera view is a south-facing 3/4 view, and there is no isometric side face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a purple void-edge floating platform with cliff lips, drawn in a locked dark purple palette. Hue is not judged. It shows about 4 visible lightness steps: a bright lip highlight, a mid purple top, a dark rock face and a deep void. Its 5 visible tones per tile beat the grass reference (3) and are below the paving reference (7). Near-flat coverage is 5%, so there is little flat fill. The stippled rock speckle and the cliff-face rubble give some texture, but they are sparse and uniform, closer to noise than to per-stone shading like the paving. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans purple and counts as a dark material tone. The structure is reasonable, but the shading ramps are shallower than the 5-6 steps in the Beodeul references, and the cliff face is simple with few distinct stones. It sits slightly below the references on density and ramp depth.

answer.evidence: The terrain block is a large dark-purple plateau. Its textured top fills rows 18-90 and ends in light front-edge lines, for example row 90 on the left and row 78-79 at the x=64 scan. Below each edge line a rocky cliff face hangs down and fades into the void background, giving a front face of about 20 rows. The notches have their own ledge lines (rows 46 and 78) with cliff faces below. The silhouette fills the whole 128-px width, and the stepped ledges look like a normal 3/4 cliff autotile, not a flat slab.
